   "source": [
    "# Workflow: Implementing a simple shield for a gymnasium environment\n",
    "\n",
    "**What is the motivation?**\n",
    "\n",
    "Shielding is a common technique in safe reinforcement learning. \n",
    "A shield blocks actions that are considered unsafe. \n",
    "There are various ways to define a shield.\n",
    "In this workflow, we construct a discretized abstraction from a continuous simulation environment.\n",
    "In the abstraction, we use action values derived using probabilistic model checking to block actions that have a too large probability of leading to unsafe states.\n",
    "Specifically, we implement a memoryless post-shield, which is close in spirit to what was used in Jansen et al. (2020), and more recently by Brorholt et al. (2026) based on learned model estimates.\n",
    "We then map the abstract shield back to the continuous environment, to use during RL training.\n",
    "To derive and deploy such shields on continuous simulation-based environments is a substantial engineering effort that `VeriGym` makes easy.\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "**What do we show here?**\n",
    "\n",
    "We show how to use `VeriGym` to compute and deploy a conceptually simple shield for a continuous `gymnasium` environment. \n",
    "As the example we use the `CartPole-v1` environment, where the task is to learn how to move left and right in order to balance a pole on a cart.\n",
    "For this task, we consider it `\"unsafe\"` to move too close to the edges of the screen, which we express using state labels on the original environment.\n",
    "Then, the workflow proceeds as follows:\n",
    "- We learn a finite-state representation of `CartPole`.\n",
    "- We model check the learned MDP using `stormpy` for the worst-case probability of reaching `\"unsafe\"` states.\n",
    "- Based on the model checking results, we compute state-action values, and construct a shield that blocks all actions that have a probability `p>0.1` of reaching an unsafe state.\n",
    "- We apply the abstract shield to the original environment using a convenience environment wrapper, that takes care of mapping the shield back to the original state space.\n",
    "- Then, we train two Reinforcement Learning agents, one shielded and one non-shielded, using the `PPO` algorithm from stable baselines.\n",
    "\n",
    "We evaluate the training development, but more importantly, we evaluate both RL agents in both the shielded and non-shielded environment, and compare episode rewards and the number of safety violations."
   ]
  },

    "def get_interval_abstraction_mapper(bins_per_state_dim, env):\n",
    "\n",
    "    bin_edges = generate_box_bins(env.observation_space, np.linspace, bins_per_state_dim)\n",
    "    state_abstraction_map = bin_edges_map(env.observation_space, bin_edges, backward_kind=\"interval\")\n",
    "    state_abstraction_map.forward_map = bin_edges.orig_to_enum\n",
    "    state_abstraction_map.original_to_enum = bin_edges.orig_to_enum\n",
    "\n",
    "    state_abstraction_map.backward_map= bin_edges.enum_to_interval\n",
    "\n",
    "    abstraction_mapper = AbstractionMapper(\n",
    "        state_abstraction_map=state_abstraction_map,\n",
    "        action_abstraction_map=AbstractionMap.initialize_identity_map(env.action_space)\n",
    "    )\n",
    "    return abstraction_mapper"
   ]
  },

    "def eval_reward_safety_violations(env, policy, unsafe_label, seed=SEED):\n",
    "    count_violations = []\n",
    "    eval_rewards = []\n",
    "    for i in range(500):\n",
    "        ep_count = 0\n",
    "        ep_reward = 0\n",
    "\n",
    "        obs, _ = env.reset(seed=seed+i)\n",
    "\n",
    "        while True:\n",
    "            action = policy.get_action(obs)\n",
    "            obs, rew, term, trunc, _ = env.step(action)\n",
    "            ep_reward += rew\n",
    "            try:\n",
    "                if unsafe_label in env.get_labels_of_state(obs):\n",
    "                    ep_count += 1\n",
    "            except:\n",
    "                if unsafe_label in env.env.get_labels_of_state(obs):\n",
    "                    ep_count += 1\n",
    "            if term or trunc:\n",
    "                break\n",
    "\n",
    "        eval_rewards.append(ep_reward)\n",
    "        count_violations.append(ep_count)\n",
    "        \n",
    "    return eval_rewards, count_violations"
   ]
  },

    "## The actual workflow"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "f4011ec8",
   "metadata": {
    "papermill": {
     "duration": 0.00378,
     "end_time": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.323644+00:00",

     "status": "completed"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "We are using the `CartPole-v1` environment in this workflow.\n",
    "We first load it from Gymnasium and then into `VeriGym`, and place bounds on unbounded dimensions of the observation space.\n",
    "This is necessary for us to be able to apply discretization techniques afterwards."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 6,
   "id": "df898cd6",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.332484Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.332069Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.342046Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.340769Z"
    },
    "papermill": {
     "duration": 0.015515,
     "end_time": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.343133+00:00",
     "exception": false,
     "start_time": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.327618+00:00",
     "status": "completed"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "gym_env = gym.make(GYM_STRING)\n",
    "gym_env = ReplaceInfObservation(gym_env, neg_inf=-5, pos_inf=5)\n",
    "env = verigym.GenerativeEnv.from_gymnasium(gym_env)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "1671a7df",
   "metadata": {
    "papermill": {
     "duration": 0.003328,
     "end_time": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.350124+00:00",
     "exception": false,
     "start_time": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.346796+00:00",
     "status": "completed"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "In this workflow, we want to construct a shield that blocks \"unsafe\" actions.\n",
    "For this, we need to define what we mean by \"unsafe\". \n",
    "Here, we consider it unsafe for the cart to move too close to the edges of the environment.\n",
    "We define this by creating a `StateLabel` object and adding it to the environment."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 7,
   "id": "796377fc",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.359029Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.358599Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.364158Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.362720Z"
    },
    "papermill": {
     "duration": 0.011392,
     "end_time": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.364878+00:00",
     "exception": false,
     "start_time": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.353486+00:00",
     "status": "completed"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "unsafe_label = StateLabel(\"unsafe\",\n",
    "                          lambda s: (s[0] < -1.5) | (s[0] > 1.5))\n",
    "env.add_state_label(unsafe_label)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "7de4b855",
   "metadata": {
    "papermill": {
     "duration": 0.002579,
     "end_time": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.370028+00:00",
     "exception": false,
     "start_time": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.367449+00:00",
     "status": "completed"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "Next, we define our desired state-space discretization and learn an abstract representation of the environment.\n",
    "In this case, we divide each dimension of the state space into 10 bins. \n",
    "To properly translate the \"unsafe\" state label to the abstract environment, we need our abstraction map to provide us with an interval type backward mapping. That means that for each bin, the backward mapping provides us with the upper and lower bin edges.\n",
    "Then, we learn the model representation by exploring randomly for `1e6` steps and aggregating transitions.\n",
    "\n",
    "This process - simulation, discretization and learning - usually takes less than 30 seconds in total."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 8,
   "id": "eaca6d4c",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.378574Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.378174Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.017562Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.016143Z"
    },
    "papermill": {
     "duration": 36.646005,
     "end_time": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.019284+00:00",
     "exception": false,
     "start_time": "2026-10-15T19:04:57.373279+00:00",
     "status": "completed"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "abstraction_mapper = get_interval_abstraction_mapper(bins_per_state_dim=10, env=env)\n",
    "\n",
    "abstracted_model = verigym.create_abstraction(\n",
    "    original_env=env,\n",
    "    abstraction_mapper=abstraction_mapper,\n",
    "    exploration_policy=RandomizedPolicy(env),\n",
    "    num_steps=int(1e6),\n",
    "    seed=SEED\n",
    ")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "0e33b31e",
   "metadata": {
    "papermill": {
     "duration": 0.009107,
     "end_time": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.035296+00:00",
     "exception": false,
     "start_time": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.026189+00:00",
     "status": "completed"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "We then export the learned abstract MDP to `stormpy` (the Python bindings for the Storm model checker) and model check it, again using the `stormpy` interface. \n",
    "The property `Pmin=? [F \"unsafe\"]` gives for each state the probability to reach an unsafe state under the safest policy possible in the estimated abstract MDP. \n",
    "We then compute the state-action probabilities from the state probabilities returned by probabilistic model checking by doing one step of value iteration.\n",
    "These state-action probabilities give us the probabilities under each action, in expectation over successor states, when following the safety-optimal policy afterwards.\n",
    "\n",
    "Note that these probabilities do not directly carry truth on the original simulator environment, as discretization does not yield such guarantees out of the box. Still, it is a very practical way to create a shield."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 9,
   "id": "a80bd92c",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.047252Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.047070Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.678185Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.677142Z"
    },
    "papermill": {
     "duration": 0.63961,
     "end_time": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.679968+00:00",
     "exception": false,
     "start_time": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.040358+00:00",
     "status": "completed"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "propertystr = 'Pmin=? [F \"unsafe\"]'\n",
    "stormpy_mdp = build_stormpy_mdp(abstracted_model)\n",
    "\n",
    "def get_action_values(mdp, propertystr):\n",
    "    formula = stormpy.parse_properties(propertystr)[0]\n",
    "    result = stormpy.check_model_sparse(mdp, formula)\n",
    "    state_values = result.get_values()\n",
    "\n",
    "    action_values = np.zeros((mdp.nr_states, len(mdp.choice_labeling.get_labels())))\n",
    "    action_values.shape\n",
    "\n",
    "    for state in mdp.states:\n",
    "        for action in state.actions:\n",
    "            if len(action.labels) == 0:\n",
    "                continue\n",
    "            action_idx = int(action.labels.pop())\n",
    "\n",
    "            action_value = 0.0\n",
    "            for tr in action.transitions:\n",
    "                action_value += tr.value() * state_values[tr.column]\n",
    "            action_values[state.id, action_idx] = action_value\n",
    "    return action_values\n",
    "\n",
    "action_values = get_action_values(stormpy_mdp, propertystr)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "2f3be4da",
   "metadata": {
    "papermill": {
     "duration": 0.009086,
     "end_time": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.696054+00:00",
     "exception": false,
     "start_time": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.686968+00:00",
     "status": "completed"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "Now it is time to compute the shield. We want to block all actions that have a probability `p>0.1` of reaching unsafe states. \n",
    "We define the shield as an action mask."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 10,
   "id": "7fd5fcda",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.708202Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.708026Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.711822Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.710790Z"
    },
    "papermill": {
     "duration": 0.011276,
     "end_time": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.712915+00:00",
     "exception": false,
     "start_time": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.701639+00:00",
     "status": "completed"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "def build_shield(action_values, safety_threshold):\n",
    "    shield = np.ones_like(action_values, dtype=bool)\n",
    "    shield[action_values > safety_threshold] = 0\n",
    "    return shield\n",
    "\n",
    "unsafe_threshold = 0.1\n",
    "shield = build_shield(action_values, unsafe_threshold)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "105494b6",
   "metadata": {
    "papermill": {
     "duration": 0.003887,
     "end_time": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.721060+00:00",
     "exception": false,
     "start_time": "2026-10-15T19:05:34.717173+00:00",
     "status": "completed"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "We apply the shield to the environment using the `AbstractShieldWrapper`, that is available as part of the convenience functionality in `verigym.supplements`.\n",
    "Notably, this wrapper requires discrete action spaces."

    "## Training on the original and on the shielded environment\n",
    "\n",
    "We train two RL agents using the `PPO` implementation from `stable_baselines3`.\n",
    "Training for 25000 steps usually takes around 30 seconds (e.g., on a MacBook Pro 2023 with an M3 chip and 18GB RAM). In total, these two training runs should be in the order of a minute, depending on your hardware."
   ]
  },

  },
  {

   "metadata": {

     "status": "completed"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "First, we load the trained policies back into `VeriGym` using the `SB3Policy` class and visualize their reward development during training.\n",
    "Since we do not train for a long time, the development looks relatively unstable for both agents, but reaches a high reward towards the end.\n",
    "\n",
    "Then, we run evaluation episodes in four different settings: \n",
    "1) default baseline: policy trained without a shield deployed on the unshielded environment\n",
    "2) post-shielding: policy trained without a shield deployed on the shielded environment\n",
    "3) pre-shielding: policy trained with shield deployed on the unshielded environment\n",
    "4) full-shielding: policy trained with shield deployed on the shielded environment\n",
    "\n",
    "We compare the output rewards and safety violations for all settings."
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "For rewards in evaluation episodes we make the following observations.\n",
    "\n",
    "- The policies that are deployed on the non-shielded environment achieve the highest reward. That indicates that the shield blocks actions with positive reward in execution. \n",
    "- However, both shielded and unshielded agent perform similarly in evaluation. That indicates that the shield does not inhibit the learning process strongly.\n",
    "- The policies that are deployed on the shielded environment achieve lower rewards. Interestingly, the agent that was shielded during training performs better than the agent that was trained without a shield."
   ]
  },
